concepts.title: LLM ทำงานอย่างไร: Token, Next-token Prediction และ Context Window
concepts.covers: Teaches: what an LLM is (pre-training + instruction tuning, not a database lookup); Token and tokenization (Thai usually costs more tokens than English for the same meaning); next-token prediction as a probability distribution; sampling and why the same prompt gives different answers; temperature/top_p/top_k as BACKGROUND ONLY (claude-opus-5-5 returns 400 if sent, and anthropic 1.15.0 messages.create no longer even has these params; steer with prompt + effort instead); context window counts system + history + documents + answer; the API is stateless (resend history every call); stop_reason values (end_turn, max_tokens, refusal, model_context_window_exceeded); why models hallucinate (plausible not true, knowledge cutoff, no internet without tools). Code: c01_next_token.py — pure-Python toy next-token model using the SAME numbers as Part 1 Step 1: context 'ร้านนี้กาแฟ' -> อร่อย 0.55, หอม 0.25, แพง 0.15, ขม 0.05; show greedy choice vs 5 samples with random.Random(seed=42) to show variation; simulate a context window by keeping only the last 8 tokens of a token list and printing what was dropped; then import llm.ask/MODE/MODEL and ask 'อธิบายว่า Token คืออะไร ใน 2 ประโยค สำหรับมือใหม่' printing mode, text, stop_reason and token counts (mock counts must be labelled as rough estimates). Show the prompt in a tpl block.

concepts.title: กายวิภาคของ Prompt ที่ดี: Role, Task, Context, Constraints, Output Format และ Examples
concepts.covers: Teaches the 6 parts of a prompt and when a part can be omitted; system prompt vs user message (role goes in the system parameter); separating sections with headings or XML tags. Code: c02_anatomy.py — a dict PARTS with keys role/task/context/constraints/output_format/examples for the task 'เขียนประกาศแจ้งปิดปรับปรุงระบบสั่งซื้อออนไลน์ของร้านกาแฟบ้านสมชาย คืนวันเสาร์ที่ 24 ต.ค. 2026 เวลา 22:00–02:00'; build_prompt(parts) returns (system, user_prompt) with each non-role part wrapped in XML tags (<task>, <context>, <constraints>, <output_format>, <examples>); check_parts(parts) prints which of the 6 parts are present/missing, run on both the full dict and a vague one-line prompt ('เขียนประกาศปิดระบบให้หน่อย'); then send via llm.ask(user_prompt, system=system, mock=...) and print the mock announcement. Show the assembled prompt in a tpl block.

concepts.title: ชัดเจนและเฉพาะเจาะจง: เทียบ Prompt แย่กับ Prompt ที่ปรับแล้ว
concepts.covers: Teaches the golden rule (show the prompt to a colleague with no context), replacing vague words with measurable constraints, positive instructions instead of prohibitions plus the reason behind each rule, long material first and instruction last, and the Thai tip of always stating the output language and register. Code: c03_bad_vs_good.py — ARTICLE: a ~120-word Thai article on 'การสำรองข้อมูลแบบ 3-2-1' (3 copies, 2 media types, 1 off-site/Cloud); BAD = 'สรุปบทความนี้ให้หน่อย'; GOOD = exactly the improved prompt from Part 1 Step 3 (audience: พนักงานร้านกาแฟที่ไม่มีพื้นฐานไอที, board notice readable in 30 seconds, Thai with English tech terms, exactly 3 bullets of <=25 words, must explain 3, 2 and 1, final line starting 'สิ่งที่ต้องทำ:'). Mock answers: BAD -> one long paragraph that mixes English and never gives an action; GOOD -> 3 bullets + 'สิ่งที่ต้องทำ:' line. A measure(text) function prints chars, bullet count, whether '3','2','1' are explained and whether 'สิ่งที่ต้องทำ:' exists; print a side-by-side comparison table. Both prompts shown as tpl blocks.

concepts.title: Context, Audience, Success Criteria และ Role Prompting: ใช้ AI เป็นติวเตอร์
concepts.covers: Teaches giving purpose/context, writing for a specific audience, defining checkable success criteria (which later become eval checks), role prompting through the system prompt (role alone is not enough), and using AI as a tutor responsibly (hints before answers, ask it to quiz you, verify with official docs, never paste keys or personal data; link the study system with Master Roadmap หัวข้อ 0.12 วิธีเรียนให้ได้ผล (Study System)). Code: c04_tutor.py — the learner question 'ทำไมโค้ดนี้ขึ้น IndexError: list index out of range' with buggy code scores=[80, 65, 90]; for i in range(len(scores) + 1): print(scores[i]); ask twice: (1) no system prompt, (2) TUTOR_SYSTEM = the exact tutor system prompt from Part 1 Step 4 (hint first, one question back, full solution only when the learner types 'ขอเฉลย', Thai with English terms, <=120 words). A check_criteria(answer) function verifies: contains a question mark, contains no full corrected loop/code block, is in Thai, and is <=600 characters; print PASS/FAIL per criterion for both mock answers (mock 1 dumps the full fixed code; mock 2 gives a hint and asks a question).

concepts.title: Prompt Template และตัวแปรใน Python กับไฟล์ YAML
concepts.covers: Teaches why templates (reuse, consistency, review prompts in PRs), the three ways to fill variables (f-string, str.format, string.Template) and the brace pitfall when a prompt contains a JSON example (show the real KeyError from str.format), Template.substitute (raises KeyError on a missing variable) vs safe_substitute, storing prompts in YAML loaded with yaml.safe_load (never yaml.load without a Loader), YAML block literal '|' and spaces-not-tabs, validating required variables against the 'variables' list with a clear Thai error (fail fast), and versioning v1/v2 files with git diff. Install: python3 -m pip install "pyyaml==6.0.3". Files: prompts/explain_error/v1.yaml (EXACTLY the YAML in Part 1 Step 5: name explain_error, version v1, variables [tool, error_text], system + template using <error tool="$tool">$error_text</error> and a 3-part answer) and c05_templates.py which renders it for 3 errors: (bash, 'bash: ./backup.sh: Permission denied'), (git, 'fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git'), (python, "ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yaml'"), then sends one through llm.ask with a mock answer; also demo the missing-variable error. Optionally show v2.yaml and the git diff output.

concepts.title: Few-shot Examples: สอนด้วยตัวอย่าง
concepts.covers: Teaches zero-shot vs one-shot vs few-shot, choosing 3–5 relevant and diverse examples that cover edge cases (sarcasm, mixed, no opinion), how strongly examples bias label/length/style, wrapping examples in <examples><example> tags, a fixed label set and 'answer with the label only', measuring accuracy on a labelled test set that does NOT overlap the examples (data leakage), and dynamic few-shot as an idea for later. Code: c06_few_shot.py — labels บวก/ลบ/กลาง for reviews of ร้านกาแฟบ้านสมชาย; the 3 examples are EXACTLY those in Part 1 Step 6 ('เมล็ดคั่วกลางหอมมาก ส่งไวด้วย จะสั่งอีกแน่นอน'->บวก, 'ดีมากเลยค่ะ รอของสองอาทิตย์ เปิดมาถุงขาด'->ลบ (sarcasm), 'ได้รับของแล้วครับ ยังไม่ได้ลองชง'->กลาง); 8 NEW labelled test reviews; zero-shot mock answers are inconsistent free text (e.g. 'Positive', 'เชิงบวกค่ะ', 'ค่อนข้างดี', one sarcasm misread) while few-shot mock answers are exact labels (realistically 7/8 or 8/8); compute and print accuracy and valid-label rate for both. Template uses string.Template with $review. Show the few-shot prompt in a tpl block.

concepts.title: Structured Output: XML Tags และ JSON Schema
concepts.covers: Teaches why code-consumed output needs structure, XML tags to separate instructions/data/answer (<instructions>, <message>, <answer>), JSON Schema with Structured Outputs via output_config={"format": {"type": "json_schema", "schema": SCHEMA}} with "additionalProperties": False then json.loads, the Pydantic helper client.messages.parse(..., output_format=Order) -> response.parsed_output (pydantic 2.14.1, real mode only), schema design (enum, required, null for unknown instead of guessing), always validating with jsonschema 4.26.0, checking stop_reason before parsing (max_tokens = truncated JSON, refusal), and that assistant prefill (starting the answer with '{') returns 400 on claude-opus-5-5. Install: python3 -m pip install "jsonschema==4.26.0" "pydantic==2.14.1". Code: c07_structured.py — extract an order from the Thai LINE chat 'สวัสดีค่ะ ชื่อมะลินะคะ ขอสั่งเมล็ดคั่วกลาง 2 ถุง กับดริปแบ็ก 1 กล่อง ส่งวันเสาร์ที่ 24 ต.ค. ได้ไหมคะ' into {customer_name, items:[{name, qty:int}], delivery_date: 'YYYY-MM-DD' or null} (2026-10-24 is a Saturday); prompt is the Part 1 Step 7 template (data is not instructions, null when no date); mock returns a valid JSON string -> validate OK; then a broken mock (qty as "2" string or missing delivery_date) -> print the real jsonschema ValidationError message.

concepts.title: งานซับซ้อน: Thinking, Effort และ Prompt Chaining
concepts.covers: Teaches that current Claude models think internally (on claude-opus-5-5 thinking is always on; thinking={'type':'disabled'} and budget_tokens return 400), effort via output_config={"effort": ...} with levels low/medium/high/xhigh/max (default medium; higher = deeper, slower, more output tokens incl. thinking = more cost), why old 'think step by step' tricks are no longer the main tool (give criteria and a self-check instead), prompt chaining (output of step N wrapped in tags becomes input of step N+1), decomposition patterns (extract -> transform -> verify, parallel steps, review step), gate checks between steps, and single call vs chain trade-offs. Code: c08_chain.py — MEETING_NOTES: Thai meeting notes of ร้านกาแฟบ้านสมชาย (launch a new menu 'ลาเต้มะพร้าว', tasks for สมชาย/ก้อง/แพร, one task without a deadline); step 1 extract facts into <facts> (effort low), gate: regex must find <facts>...</facts> else stop with a clear Thai message; step 2 draft email in <email> using the Part 1 Step 8 template (effort medium, '(ยังไม่กำหนด)' for missing deadline); step 3 review against a checklist (effort high) returning <review>; print each step's output and per-step/total token usage (mock estimates labelled). Include a flag or second run that feeds a malformed step-1 mock to show the gate stopping the chain.

concepts.title: เอกสารยาว Grounding และการลด Hallucination
concepts.covers: Teaches long-document prompting (documents first, question last), <document index> with <source> and <document_content>, quote-then-answer (<quotes> then <answer>), explicitly allowing 'ไม่พบข้อมูลในเอกสาร', requiring citations like [ข้อ 3], restricting to provided knowledge, code-based grounding check (every quote must be an exact substring of the document), second-pass verification, and strategies for documents longer than the context window (chunking, map-reduce, RAG -> topic 11). Code: c09_grounded_qa.py — POLICY = 'นโยบายการคืนสินค้า ร้านกาแฟบ้านสมชาย (ฉบับ ต.ค. 2026)' with 10 numbered clauses (e.g. return within 7 days of receipt, unopened seal only, opened drip bags not returnable, customer pays return shipping unless damaged in transit, report via LINE Official with photos, refund within 5 business days); prompt = Part 1 Step 9 template; 3 questions: one directly answerable, one combining 2 clauses, one not in the document ('ส่งคืนสินค้าจากต่างประเทศได้ไหม' -> 'ไม่พบข้อมูลในเอกสาร' + contact LINE Official); parse <quotes>/<answer> with regex; verify_quotes() prints FOUND/NOT FOUND per quote; include one mock answer from an ungrounded v1 prompt with a fabricated quote ('คืนสินค้าได้ภายใน 30 วัน') that the checker flags.

concepts.title: ประเมิน Prompt: Test Cases, Automated Checks, LLM-as-judge และ Version Control
concepts.covers: Teaches why vibe checks are not evidence and how regressions happen, designing test cases (normal, edge, adversarial; separate from few-shot examples) stored in YAML, code-based checks (keyword, regex, max length, JSON parse + schema, exact match), rubric-based LLM-as-judge returning JSON {score 1-5, reason} with a deterministic mock judge, validating the judge against human labels and its biases (length, position), metrics (pass rate per version and per check, mean judge score), running each case several times in real mode, never changing prompt and test set in the same round, and git workflow (results in commit message, git tag summarize_ticket-v2, git revert on regression). Code: c10_eval.py + cases.yaml with 10 cases for the 'summarize_ticket' prompt (customer support ticket -> JSON {"summary": str <=120 chars, "category": enum delivery|product|payment|account|other, "urgent": bool}); prompts v1 (vague) and v2 (specific + schema); per-version mock outputs keyed by case id; checks keyword/regex/max_chars/json_schema + judge using the Part 1 Step 10 rubric template; print a comparison table v1 vs v2 with pass rates, write results/v1.json and results/v2.json, then show git add/commit/tag commands with a results-bearing commit message.

concepts.title: Prompt Injection และความปลอดภัย
concepts.covers: Teaches direct vs indirect prompt injection, why it cannot be fully prevented (instructions and data share one token stream) so defense in depth, prompt-level defenses (rules in system prompt, external data in tags declared as data not instructions, narrow output schema with a 'suspicious' flag), system-level defenses (least privilege, human approval for destructive actions, output validation with allowlists, no secrets in prompts, canary tokens for testing), adding attacks to the eval set, PII masking, handling stop_reason 'refusal', and ethics (test only your own apps; พ.ร.บ.ว่าด้วยการกระทำความผิดเกี่ยวกับคอมพิวเตอร์) in a sec callout. Code: c11_injection.py — customer-email summarizer for ร้านกาแฟบ้านสมชาย; NAIVE prompt concatenates the email; DEFENDED prompt = Part 1 Step 11 system prompt + <email> tags + JSON {summary, suspicious}; canary 'CANARY-7F3A' placed in the system prompt for leak testing only; 6 test emails: 4 attacks (direct 'ลืมคำสั่งก่อนหน้า', instructions hidden in an HTML comment, request for a 100% discount code, injected link https://evil.example) + 2 benign; mock NAIVE leaks/obeys in 3 of 4 attacks, DEFENDED leaks 0 and flags suspicious; validate_output() rejects any output containing the canary or a URL not in ALLOWLIST; print a results table and leak rate per version.

concepts.title: Prompt ภาษาไทย ต้นทุน Token และ Prompt Caching
concepts.covers: Teaches Thai prompting tips (always state output language, keep technical terms in English, set register ครับ/ค่ะ and formality, specify พ.ศ./ค.ศ., Arabic vs Thai digits, date and money formats, instructions in Thai vs English decided by eval), Thai tokenization cost measured with client.messages.count_tokens(...).input_tokens in real mode only (free per docs as of Oct 2026 but rate-limited; never tiktoken), cost formula and per-model prices (output is 5x input; thinking counts as output so higher effort costs more), cost-reduction tactics, and prompt caching: top-level cache_control={"type": "ephemeral"} on messages.create, verify via usage.cache_creation_input_tokens and usage.cache_read_input_tokens, prefix rules (stable content first, no timestamps in system prompt), minimum cacheable length roughly 512–4096 tokens (shorter prefix silently not cached), TTL 5m default, 1h option. Code: c12_cost_cache.py — (1) the same sentence in Thai and English: real mode prints count_tokens results; mock mode prints llm.rough_tokens estimates clearly labelled 'ค่าประมาณในโหมดจำลอง ไม่ใช่ค่าจริง' (never present invented counts as real); (2) cost table reusing PRICES from Part 1 Step 12 cost.py (1,000 calls x 1,500 input + 300 output tokens -> claude-opus-5-5 $12.00, claude-sonnet-5-5 $6.00, claude-haiku-5-5 $0.30 per day); (3) caching demo calling llm.CLIENT.messages.create directly in real mode with a long stable system prompt (product catalog + policy) twice and printing the cache usage fields; in mock mode print fixed sample usage numbers labelled '[MOCK] ตัวเลขจำลอง'. Show the Thai-spec tpl block from Part 1 Step 12.

mini_project.name: Prompt Library + Evaluation Harness
mini_project.summary: A git-versioned library of prompt templates stored as YAML, plus a Python evaluation harness that runs every prompt version against YAML test cases with automated checks (keyword, regex, JSON schema, max length) and an LLM-as-judge rubric. It runs in mock mode with no API key (reading recorded answers per prompt version and case id) and in real mode against Claude, then prints a comparison report between prompt versions. The repo lives at ~/projects/prompt-library and is pushed to GitHub as 'prompt-library'.
mini_project.features: 1) Prompt library: prompts/classify_feedback/v1.yaml and v2.yaml (Thai customer feedback for ร้านกาแฟบ้านสมชาย -> JSON {"category": enum delivery|product|service|price|other, "sentiment": enum บวก|ลบ|กลาง, "summary_th": str}) and prompts/summarize_ticket/v1.yaml and v2.yaml (support ticket -> JSON {"summary": str <=120 chars, "category": enum delivery|product|payment|account|other, "urgent": bool}). Each YAML has name, version, description, variables, system, template (string.Template $vars), optional output_schema. v1 is deliberately vague; v2 adds role, XML-tagged data, few-shot examples and schema. 2) Test cases: cases/classify_feedback.yaml and cases/summarize_ticket.yaml, about 8–10 cases each (normal, edge, adversarial/injection), each with id (e.g. fb-001, tk-001), vars, and a checks list. 3) Five check types in harness/checks.py and harness/judge.py: keyword (all/any/none), regex, json_schema (jsonschema 4.26.0), max_chars, judge (rubric prompt returning {score, reason}; deterministic mock judge in mock mode; pass if score >= min_score). Each check returns (passed: bool, reason: str in Thai). 4) Modes: harness/llm.py make_client(); mock when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is missing, reading mocks//.yaml keyed by case id; real mode uses anthropic==1.15.0 with MODEL from CLAUDE_MODEL (default claude-opus-5-5), checks stop_reason, handles errors most-specific-first. 5) CLI: python3 run_eval.py classify_feedback --versions v1 v2 [--runs N for real mode] [--threshold 0.8]; prints per-case PASS/FAIL table per version, per-check failure reasons, pass rate per version and the winner; writes results/_.json (results/ is git-ignored); exits non-zero when the latest version's pass rate is below the threshold (CI-ready). 6) tests/test_checks.py with pytest 9.1.1 covering every check type, no key needed. 7) Git workflow: .gitignore (.venv/, .env, __pycache__/, results/), .env.example without a real key, one commit per prompt version with results in the message (e.g. 'classify_feedback v2: add 3 examples + schema, pass 9/10 (v1: 5/10)'), git tag classify_feedback-v2, verification that git log --all -- .env prints nothing, README with results table and how to run mock/real mode, push to GitHub (link ). Extension ideas: GitHub Actions running pytest + mock eval on every PR, multiple runs per case in real mode with variance, a cheaper-model comparison (claude-haiku-5-5 vs claude-opus-5-5) with cost per run, an HTML/Markdown report, prompt caching for the judge rubric.
mini_project.stack: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS on WSL2; Python 3.12.3 (system python3) in a venv .venv; anthropic==1.15.0; pyyaml==6.0.3; jsonschema==4.26.0; pytest==9.1.1; python-dotenv==1.2.4 (optional); Git 2.43.0 + GitHub. Models: claude-opus-5-5 (default, via CLAUDE_MODEL env var), claude-haiku-5-5 optional for cost comparison. Exact folder tree (already shown in Part 1 Step 13, Part 4 must match): prompt-library/{.gitignore, .env.example, README.md, requirements.txt, run_eval.py, harness/{__init__.py, llm.py, loader.py, checks.py, judge.py, report.py}, prompts/{classify_feedback/{v1.yaml,v2.yaml}, summarize_ticket/{v1.yaml,v2.yaml}}, cases/{classify_feedback.yaml, summarize_ticket.yaml}, mocks/{classify_feedback/{v1.yaml,v2.yaml}, summarize_ticket/{v1.yaml,v2.yaml}}, tests/test_checks.py}.

versions: All tested in the sandbox on 2026-10-19 (sandbox Python 3.13; code must target Python 3.12+). Ubuntu 24.04 LTS on WSL2; Python 3.12.3 (system python3; packages only inside `python3 -m venv .venv`, install with `python3 -m pip install "pkg==x.y.z"`); Git 2.43.0. PyPI pins: anthropic==1.15.0 (latest; 1.x needs Python 3.10+), pyyaml==6.0.3, jsonschema==4.26.0, pydantic==2.14.1, python-dotenv==1.2.4 (optional), pytest==9.1.1. Do NOT use tiktoken. Models (exact IDs, no date suffix): claude-opus-5-5 (default; MODEL = os.environ.get("CLAUDE_MODEL", "claude-opus-5-5")), claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-haiku-5-5. Prices per 1M tokens input/output: Opus 5.5 $4/$20, Sonnet 5.5 $2/$10, Haiku 5.5 $0.10/$0.50 (prompts up to 100K tokens); always add "ราคา ณ ต.ค. 2026 ตรวจสอบล่าสุดที่หน้า Pricing ของผู้ให้บริการ". Verified in anthropic 1.15.0: messages.create has NO temperature/top_p/top_k parameters; output_config keys are effort (low|medium|high|xhigh|max, default medium on Opus 5.5) and format (json_schema); messages.parse(output_format=PydanticModel) -> response.parsed_output; messages.count_tokens(model, messages, system).input_tokens; top-level cache_control={"type":"ephemeral"} (ttl "5m" default or "1h"); usage fields input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens; stop_reason literals end_turn, max_tokens, stop_sequence, tool_use, pause_turn, refusal, model_context_window_exceeded. On claude-opus-5-5 these return 400: temperature/top_p/top_k, thinking={"type":"disabled"}, budget_tokens, assistant prefill, tool_choice any/tool. Error handling order: AuthenticationError, RateLimitError, APIStatusError (e.status_code), APIConnectionError; SDK retries 429/5xx (max_retries=2). The sandbox reaches api.anthropic.com: running with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-fake really raises AuthenticationError, so the error path can be tested. Ollama and @anthropic-ai/sdk: mention only, no version (tell learners to check ollama.com / npm).

Part 2 files: c01_next_token.py, c02_anatomy.py, c03_bad_vs_good.py, c04_tutor.py, c05_templates.py (+ prompts/explain_error/v1.yaml, v2.yaml), c06_few_shot.py, c07_structured.py, c08_chain.py, c09_grounded_qa.py, c10_eval.py (+ cases.yaml, results/), c11_injection.py, c12_cost_cache.py, plus cost.py from Part 1 Step 12. SHARED HELPER llm.py (Part 2 setup section must create it; Part 1 Step 2 says it exists; tested in mock mode and with a fake key). Interface: MODEL; Reply dataclass(text, stop_reason, input_tokens, output_tokens, mode); make_client() returns anthropic.Anthropic() if ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set, else None; CLIENT; MODE = "real"|"mock"; rough_tokens(text) = max(1, len(text)//3) (mock-only rough estimate, must be labelled as an estimate); ask(prompt, *, system=None, mock="[MOCK] ไม่มีคำตอบจำลองสำหรับ Prompt นี้", max_tokens=2048, effort=None, output_config=None) -> Reply (mock path returns Reply(mock, "end_turn", rough_tokens(system+prompt), rough_tokens(mock), "mock"); real path builds kwargs model/max_tokens/messages, adds system, merges effort into output_config, calls CLIENT.messages.create, catches AuthenticationError -> SystemExit("API Key ไม่ถูกต้อง ตรวจค่า ANTHROPIC_API_KEY อีกครั้ง"), RateLimitError, APIStatusError (status_code), APIConnectionError, joins text blocks); count_tokens(text, system=None) -> int or None in mock mode. Every script prints a first line like "โหมด: mock | โมเดล: claude-opus-5-5". Tested output of a first call in mock mode: "stop_reason=end_turn input=16 output=55" style lines. c12 calls llm.CLIENT.messages.create directly for cache_control. Never print the API key.
